extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and peer reviewers for NIH SBIR Phase II (Type 2 R42/R44) biomedical grant applications; PI and institutional grants staff
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review criteria and committee guidance used to evaluate NIH SBIR Phase II (R42/R44) grant applications in biomedical research, including scientific, ethical, resource, and budgetary standards. The page is a Summary Statement documenting criterion scores, reviewer comments, and administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the project addresses an important problem or critical barrier in the field and whether successful completion would have a significant impact on scientific knowledge, technical capability, or clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite strengths such as the public health importance of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, lack of existing vaccine, and the scientific premise established in Phase I; weaknesses are noted when none exist. Example strengths listed: disease prevalence, antibiotic resistance urgency, and prior data supporting premise. Score reported (example): Significance: 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the qualifications, productivity, and suitability of the project team to execute the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer evidence includes prior accomplishments (e.g., discovery of IL-12 effect), complementary expertise among collaborators, and track record of completing Phase I aims. Weaknesses may note unclear need for multiple PIs. Score reported (example): Investigator(s): 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the application challenges current paradigms, employs novel concepts or methods, or modifies existing approaches in innovative ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from reviewers: discovery that IL-12 can convert infection into a vaccine and co-delivery with OMVs via nanoparticle sustained-release is innovative. Scores given (examples): Innovation: 1–2. Reviewers explicitly list 'None noted' for weaknesses when innovation is strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the overall strategy, methodology, feasibility, identification of potential problems and alternative strategies, statistical rigor, and experimental design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer guidance and examples: strong approaches include clear comparisons of routes (intranasal vs intravaginal), well-defined animal models, replication of experiments, planned preclinical safety testing, and attention to pitfalls/alternatives. Weaknesses highlighted include inadequate backup plans (e.g., if detergent-extracted OMVs lose protective lipoproteins), unclear rationale for some dosing routes (e.g., IL-12 IV), and need for better-defined power calculations. Score reported (example): Approach: 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges whether the institutional support, equipment, and other resources are adequate to ensure project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note 'Excellent environment' or list available resources and equipment as strengths; absence of environment-related weaknesses is explicitly noted. Score reported (example): Environment: 1–2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements synthesize criterion scores and comments into an overall impact judgement (textual justification provided). Administrative note: overall impact scores are averaged across voting reviewers (1–9) and multiplied by 10 to yield the impact/priority score; criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not themselves calculated into the overall impact score during discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Relevant Biological Variables (e.g., sex as a biological variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the application appropriately considers biological variables such as sex that may affect study outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers explicitly mention when sex as a biological variable is 'appropriately addressed' or note limitations (e.g., protective immunity experiments proposed in female mice only due to lack of male model). Guidance includes repeating experiments in males if intranasal immunization generates systemic responses. This is part of Approach and Rigor assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Rigor and Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether experiments are designed and described to ensure reproducible, rigorous results (including replication, sample sizes, power calculations, and transparent methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers praised rigorous treatment of outcomes, potential difficulties, and replication plans (repeat murine experiments twice with sufficient mice). Weaknesses called out include insufficiently defined power calculations and missing authentication of key reagents. Statements such as 'The rigor and reproducibility standards have been met' are used when satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (animal welfare, justification, and experimental design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses justification for use of vertebrate animals, that the four required points for vertebrate animal review are addressed, and that experimental groups are adequately powered and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples: 'Vertebrate Animals: Acceptable' and 'YES, all four points addressed.' Reviewers may request better-defined power calculations for group sizes. Animal use and associated welfare/justification are explicitly evaluated and scored (Animal Subjects: e.g., '30-Vertebrate animals involved - no SRG concerns noted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates protections for human subjects when applicable (risk/benefit, consent, privacy, and monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no human subjects are involved, reviewers note 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)'. For clinical trials, a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan is applicable; otherwise it is 'Not Applicable (No Clinical Trials)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (for clinical trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to describe a plan for monitoring data safety for clinical trials and appropriate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applicable to clinical trials. The summary statement lists this separately and indicates 'Not Applicable' when no clinical trials are proposed. When applicable, reviewers will evaluate adequacy of monitoring plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether proposed work involves biohazards and whether appropriate precautions and containment are described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical determinations in reviewer comments are 'Biohazards: Acceptable' or identify concerns if biosafety is inadequate. Examples in this review: 'Biohazards: Acceptable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether plans for sharing research resources, data, and materials are adequate and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer determinations can be 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable.' Example weakness cited: 'No plans presented' leading to 'Resource Sharing Plans: Unacceptable.' Applicants must include clear plans for sharing where required by policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether applicants provide verification/authentication plans for key biological and chemical reagents (e.g., strains, proteins) to ensure identity and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative policy note: Applications submitted on/after Jan 25, 2016 must include a PDF attachment describing authentication plans (NOT-OD-16-011); reviewers were asked to consider that attachment in evaluation. Example critiques: 'Authentication... Unacceptable — No verification of key strains or integrity of IL-12 presented.' In some critiques this item was marked 'Acceptable' when authentication was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support (appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the proposed budget and project period are reasonable, justified, and appropriate for the scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may 'Recommend as requested' when budget is appropriate. Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and may be adjusted by Institute grants management if an award is planned; Committee Budget Recommendations section outlines recommended adjustments or confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II (Type 2 R42 and Type 2 R44) criteria / Commercialization potential
rubrics_metrics.description: For SBIR Phase II applications, reviewers evaluate whether the Phase II proposal is a logical extension of Phase I data and whether commercialization plans and scale-up considerations are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from reviewers: 'Well-conceived Phase II proposal that builds upon Phase I data'; commercialization plan described as 'well developed'; 'Acceptable' verdict for Phase II. Reviewers examine commercial potential and readiness of pre-IND preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations / Administrative Budget Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative assessment and guidance on how requested costs will be handled if an award is planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The budget in the summary is the requested amount and not yet adjusted for reviewer recommendations. Grants management staff will calculate final costs based on committee recommendations. 'Committee Budget Recommendations' and 'ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET NOTE' sections summarize this process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Impact/Priority Score Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains how reviewers' numeric scores translate into the final impact/priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1–9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting nor directly calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. See NIH peer review process documentation for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and FOIA confidentiality considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance about confidentiality of peer review materials and the handling of applications under FOIA requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will subject released materials to FOIA exemptions and may redact confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information. Summary statements are privileged communications but may be posted with permission under specified conditions.
